Date: 2026-10-07

Society & Human Rights
• France has suspended police use of stun grenades at school protests after a teenager lost a hand, amid mass nationwide demonstrations over education funding and accusations of excessive force. 
• In the US, Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike is conscious and speaking after a botched execution attempt; her lawyers are seeking preservation of evidence.
• At least 73 detained immigrants at an ICE facility in Georgia launched a hunger strike over prolonged detention and conditions.
• Indian police detained opposition leaders during protests alleging manipulation of voter rolls, escalating political tensions.
• Sri Lanka’s former first lady was arrested over alleged misuse of children’s hospital donations linked to a charity.
Why it matters: From protest policing to capital punishment and detention conditions, governments face mounting scrutiny over due process, accountability and the proportional use of force.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqzjx7z2r4gko https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/07/ice-detention-facility-georgia https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c8kgezxn54qko https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crpdgvx82831o https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck0e0n3xzvp4o

Economy & Markets
• A global bond sell-off resumed, with the US 30-year Treasury yield hitting its highest since 2002; French, Italian and UK bonds also fell in volatile trading.
• IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva warned AI is a double-edged sword—boosting growth prospects but contributing to inflation and higher yields amid elevated public debt.
• Japan’s competition authorities raided Asahi, Kirin and Suntory over alleged beer price-fixing.
• Paramount completed its $110B merger creating the Skydance behemoth, with plans to unify HBO Max and Paramount+ over time.
Why it matters: Rising yields and market concentration raise financing costs and risk, while consolidation and antitrust scrutiny shape corporate power and consumer choice.
Sources: https://www.ft.com/content/33c67aa0-bfdb-457b-84bb-960b4fed94b6 https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/07/economy-inflation-ai-trade-imf-iran-hormuz-trump-.html https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm5yn3592xk9o https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/10/paramount-completes-111b-warner-merger-creating-skydance-behemoth/

Science & Technology
• The Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai for breakthroughs explaining life’s molecular asymmetry and enabling asymmetric synthesis.
• The Nobel Physics Prize honored neutrino physicist Francis Halzen for leading development of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory.
• Samsung Wallet now supports digital car keys for select GM models in the US and Canada; Google detailed a Pixel Buds update including watch-assisted sleep detection.
• Finland ordered Google to halt work on two data centers as the country balances AI-driven infrastructure growth with local oversight.
Why it matters: Landmark science advances intersect with rapid consumer-tech evolution and infrastructure decisions that will shape the next wave of AI and connectivity.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6ly038jg0d4o https://arstechnica.com/science/2026/10/neutrino-physicist-wins-2026-nobel-physics-prize/ https://www.theverge.com/transportation/1006585/samsung-wallet-now-unlocks-some-gm-cars https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/07/google-finland-data-center-halt.html

Geopolitics & Diplomacy
• Donald Trump said he would speak to Vladimir Putin about a Russian lab worker’s suspected pneumonic plague death, prompting calls for greater transparency.
• Germany arrested former spy chief August Hanning on treason charges, a dramatic turn for the country’s intelligence establishment.
• Kosovo’s parliament elected Justina Shiroka Pula as president amid protests and political turmoil.
• The US set fresh parameters for an Iran nuclear understanding, signaling possible space for compromise but highlighting major obstacles.
Why it matters: Health biosecurity fears, espionage scandals, leadership changes and nuclear diplomacy all underscore a fraught global landscape with high stakes for stability.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqgm0vrl3xp7o https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/7/german-ex-spy-chief-arrested-for-treason-what-we-know https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/7/justina-shiroka-pula-kosovos-new-president-elected-during-a-crisis https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/7/us-sets-new-demands-for-iran-deal-what-are-they

Armed Conflict & Security
• Russia launched large-scale strikes across Ukraine, killing at least 15, as EU officials decried Moscow’s “strategy of terror.”
• Israeli strikes across Gaza continued, with reports of civilian and rescue worker casualties; Israelis marked the Oct. 7 anniversary amid revelations of prior warnings.
• Regional tensions rose: the US moved long-range bombers from the UK over a possible Iranian threat, UK authorities probed Iran-linked plots near a base, and Houthis launched missiles toward Riyadh and Aden.
• Drone attacks sank cargo ships near NATO countries’ economic zones, raising alarms over maritime security.
Why it matters: Intensifying conventional and hybrid threats—from missiles and drones to covert plots—are reshaping regional balances and straining civilian safety and commerce.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckr5ym098vdeo https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/7/israeli-attacks-across-gaza-kill-at-least-four-palestinians https://www.npr.org/2026/10/07/nx-s1-5992704/investigation-continues-into-whether-u-k-air-base-incident-is-linked-to-iran https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/10/drone-strikes-likely-russian-sink-ships-in-nato-countries-economic-zones/

Sports
• Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta signed a new deal through 2030 after ending the club’s 22-year Premier League title drought; he called it “only the beginning.”
• WADA’s president warned Kenya must bolster anti-doping enforcement to credibly host the 2029 World Athletics Championships.
• Thomas Tuchel is refining England’s approach rather than overhauling it, as the national team enters a new phase.
• Former UFC security staffer Sal Everett earned a fighter contract after a knockout win on Dana White’s Contender Series.
Why it matters: Leadership continuity, anti-doping credibility and tactical evolution shape competitive integrity and long-term success across elite sport.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/crz65j5p8l57o https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/10/7/arsenal-boss-mikel-arteta-signs-new-contract-with-premier-league-champions https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/articles/c9kgj0vj0gx4o https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cvp8gex8wzneo

Climate & Environment
• A 13-year-old Tuvaluan appealed to world leaders to act on climate change as Pacific nations push for more accessible climate finance.
• Brazil’s election gains for Flávio Bolsonaro jolted environmentalists, raising fears for Amazon protections despite recent deforestation gains under Lula.
• Google signed a 20-year deal with Constellation to upgrade six US nuclear sites to power energy-hungry data centers.
• Arctic sea ice hit its 2026 minimum, while forecasters warn of a potential Atlantic hurricane and a powerful El Niño driving extreme weather.
Why it matters: Political headwinds, financing gaps and tech-sector energy demand complicate the urgent push to cut emissions and adapt to escalating climate risks.
Sources: https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/10/7/girl-pleads-for-world-leaders-to-save-her-country-from-climate-change https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/07/flavio-bolsonaro-advance-brazil-election-jolt-climate-campaigners https://www.theverge.com/science/1006082/google-nuclear-energy-power-purchase-agreement-constellation https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/arctic-sea-ice-shrinks-to-its-2026-minimum/

Longevity & Anti-Aging
• Drugmakers say popular GLP-1 weight-loss drugs appear to slow biological aging on molecular “clocks,” though independent validation is needed.
• Early human attempts at partial epigenetic reprogramming reportedly occurred via medical tourism avenues, ahead of formal clinical readouts.
• New studies link age-related declines in autophagy to impaired senescent cell clearance, and identify mitochondrial lipid changes as drivers of dysfunction.
• Research implicates peripheral dendritic cell priming of CD8+ T cells in tau-related neurodegeneration.
Why it matters: Promising but nascent interventions are emerging across metabolism, epigenetics, and immune pathways—highlighting both therapeutic potential and the need for rigorous oversight.
Sources: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10/06/1145836/weight-loss-drugs-glp1-lilly-novo-aging-clocks/ https://www.fightaging.org/archives/2026/10/khl-foundation-reports-the-likely-first-human-partial-epigenetic-reprogramming-treatments/ https://lifespan.io/declining-autophagy-impairs-senescent-cell-clearance/ https://www.nature.com/articles/s43587-026-01254-4

Artificial Intelligence
• OpenAI released hundreds of manuscripts claiming solutions to long-standing math problems, extending AI’s push into formal reasoning and stirring debate over research norms.
• Google will restrict free Gemini users to the Flash Lite model and launched Playground, a browser platform to build games from text prompts in partnership with Unity.
• AI agents face access roadblocks from websites; industry players including Meta and Sierra are proposing standards to make bot interactions more manageable.
• Common Sense Media called ChatGPT for Teens an “unacceptable risk,” spotlighting youth safety concerns as AI enters classrooms.
• Infrastructure and adoption continue to scale, with startups raising large rounds and vendors offering credits and programs to attract builders.
Why it matters: As AI capabilities accelerate, access, safety and monetization choices will determine who benefits—and at what cost to trust, education and the open web.
Sources: https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1005004/openai-math-release-github https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1005451/google-gemini-free-flash-lite-only https://www.ft.com/content/0cb02773-d207-4920-8c74-d9707d2622a0 https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/06/the-next-hurdle-for-ai-agents-getting-websites-to-let-them-in/ https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1006355/openai-chatgpt-for-teens-common-sense-media

Entertainment
• Xbox secured rights to stream Grand Theft Auto VI via Xbox Cloud Gaming, signaling an aggressive push for cloud exclusives.
• HBO Max and Paramount+ will unify into a single service under the newly combined Skydance company following Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.
• Amazon struck a six-year deal to stream the Emmys on Prime Video starting in 2027, reportedly paying around $120 million and making the show free to watch.
• Spotify will expand its audiobooks offering to over 180 markets, adding new language catalogs.
• Independent producers of British boxing biopic “In the Shadows” will self-release in the UK after the distributor’s collapse, highlighting fragility in indie distribution.
Why it matters: Platform exclusivity and mega-mergers are redrawing media distribution, while streamers broaden offerings and indies experiment with new release paths.
Sources: https://www.theverge.com/report/1005859/microsoft-xbox-gta-6-streaming-rights https://www.theverge.com/entertainment/1005696/hbo-max-paramout-plus-merge-skydance https://www.theverge.com/entertainment/1005436/amazon-prime-video-emmys-deal https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/digital/spotify-audiobooks-2-1236723507/ https://variety.com/2026/film/global/in-the-shadows-producers-self-release-boxing-film-true-brit-1236904154/

Other
• Ars Technica promoted its ArsPro subscription, offering an improved ad-light reading experience to support independent journalism.
• Carhartt WIP and Kinto launched a modern take on the Japanese clay cooking pot (donabe), blending utility with design in a Black/Grey edition.
Why it matters: Reader-supported models and lifestyle collaborations reflect evolving strategies for sustaining media and design-forward consumer goods.
Sources: https://arstechnica.com/staff/2026/10/make-ars-better-with-an-arspro-subscription/ https://hypebeast.com/2026/10/kinto-for-carhartt-wip-kakomi-donabe-release-info

Health & Pandemic
• New Zealand’s Healthy Homes Initiative was associated with a 30% reduction in child hospitalizations over five years, according to a longitudinal analysis.
• An experimental epigenetic-editing therapy suppressed hepatitis B for at least six months in early study results, suggesting a potential path to functional cure.
• A Guardian investigation highlighted severe heat risks for US farm workers on H-2A visas, including a debilitating 2022 incident in North Carolina.
Why it matters: Targeted public health interventions, frontier antiviral approaches and stronger worker protections can materially reduce disease burden and health inequities.
Sources: https://phys.org/news/2026-10-children-homes-hospitalization-analysis.html https://singularityhub.com/2026/10/06/epigenetic-editing-could-wipe-out-lingering-hepatitis-b/ https://www.theguardian.com/environment/ng-interactive/2026/oct/07/north-carolina-farm-workers-disability-health-heat

Art & Culture
• Taiwanese director Lu Po-Shun’s debut “Will You Still Be My Friend” moved from San Sebastián to Busan with two Golden Horse nominations, blending youth, politics and solar development.
• “Concrete Land,” a debut documentary by Asmahan Bkerat, chronicles a Palestinian Bedouin family displaced in Jordan, screening at the London Film Festival.
• CAPE marked its 35th anniversary gala, celebrating Asian and Pacific Islander creatives across film, TV and media; Million Goods opened a Fort Greene venue merging menswear, hi-fi and natural wine.
Why it matters: Films centering displacement and social change, alongside community-led cultural spaces, broaden representation and sustain creative ecosystems.
Sources: https://variety.com/2026/film/festivals/will-you-still-be-my-friend-lu-po-shun-san-sebastian-busan-1236904161/ https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/concrete-land-doc-film-palestinian-bedouin-family-displaced-1236679540/ https://www.rollingstone.com/product-recommendations/lifestyle/cape-35th-anniversary-gala-randall-park-manny-jacinto-pitt-1235637366/ https://hypebeast.com/2026/10/million-goods-fort-greene-brooklyn-store-opening

Entertainment.title: LEX Models UGG®’s Fall/Winter 2026 Collection
Entertainment.text: Founded in Southern California in 1978 by an Australian surfer, UGG® introduces the Classic Micro Distort, Classic Distort Boot, and Heritage Utility Grizz as its new Fall/Winter 2026 styles. These three pairs inherit the comfort the brand has cultivated while adopting different approaches to create fresh silhouettes.UGG® has long been loved for its sheepskin boots, originally worn by surfers to warm their feet after leaving the ocean. Starting from that core of soft comfort, this latest collection reexamines the brand's staples through form and function.The Classic Micro Distort and Classic Distort Boot from the "Distort Collection," which adds a twist to familiar silhouettes, take the design codes of the iconic UGG® Classic Boot and warp, split, and expand them into something slightly uncanny. At the same time, they retain recognizable details like the twin seams and the Classic outsole, ensuring their identity as UGG® is immediately clear.The Heritage Utility Grizz combines two-tone faux fur with functional details, expressing "comfort" in a new way. Building on the cushioning, traction, and protection of the Heritage Utility tooling, it incorporates ratchet straps reminiscent of snowboard boots to create a striking contrast between soft fur and rugged hardware.For this release, Hypebeast Japan tapped rapper LEX to model in a special editorial. Inspired by the designs of the three shoes, the shoot was built around the concept of "A Familiar Strangeness," blending reality and unreality. By injecting subtle surreal elements into an initially empty space around LEX, the imagery creates a slightly mysterious world where an uncanny mood creeps into familiar scenes.Additionally, Hypebeast Japan conducted an exclusive interview with Pierce Lopatic, Sr. Director, Design - Global UGG Men's Footwear, based at the California headquarters. We dive into the design philosophy behind the Fall/Winter 2026 collection, the origins of the new items, and the deep attention paid to materials and details—uncovering the design stories that lie beneath the surface of the products.Hypebeast: How do the Classic Micro Distort, Classic Distort Boot, and Heritage Utility Grizz carry forward the UGG® DNA while evolving into new designs?For UGG®, the brand's DNA is a crucial foundation for creating anything new. In these three styles, we carried forward the comfort and heritage unique to UGG® while applying different approaches to add fresh expressions.What is the intent behind the asymmetrical stitching and distorted designs of the Classic Micro Distort and Classic Distort Boot?The Classic Micro Distort and Classic Distort Boot are our love letter to the Classic Boot. We wanted to explore how far we could evolve it while maintaining its recognition as an iconic design.Using the silhouette of the UGG® Classic Boot, the twin seams, and the Classic outsole as a base, we intentionally warped, split, and expanded the stitching, collar lines, and outsole to create a somewhat uncanny, deconstructed silhouette. Yet, we kept the presence that makes it instantly recognizable as UGG®. The goal of this design was to boldly transform an existing icon while preserving its essential identity.What new expressions or character did you hope to bring to UGG® with the Heritage Utility Grizz's distinctively voluminous silhouette and fluffy fur?With the Heritage Utility Grizz, we heavily featured two-tone faux fur to highlight the material's presence, reimagining UGG®'s "comfort" in a different form.At the same time, we aimed for a shoe that lets the wearer assert their own presence through styling. It’s a bold style where you can feel the appeal of the materials and make a statement with your footwear. I think it’s perfect for anyone looking to have fun with a bolder-than-usual shoe choice.How is the "Utility" in the Heritage Utility Grizz name expressed in the boot's design?While fur is the main feature of the Heritage Utility Grizz, what I find especially interesting is how it's paired with utility-driven details.By intentionally combining the soft texture of fur with rugged, functional elements, we created an unexpected contrast. We built upon the "Heritage Utility" tooling, which enhances cushioning, traction, and protection, and added a ratchet strap to the upper—something you'd typically see on a snowboard boot. Rather than simply following traditional codes, we blended new forms and functionality to evolve the look into something unprecedented while retaining the UGG® feel.The Classic Micro Distort is priced at ¥35,200 and the Classic Distort Boot at ¥44,000, both available in Chestnut and Black. The Heritage Utility Grizz is ¥44,000. All styles are currently available at the UGG® official online store, UGG® Tokyo Flagship Store, UGG® Ginza Matsuya-dori, and UGG® Osaka (Heritage Utility Grizz only). Be sure to check them out. Entertainment.title: H. Moser & Cie. Gives Retrograde Seconds Three Different Personalities
Entertainment.text: SummaryH. Moser & Cie. expands its retrograde seconds complication across three collections.Pioneer, Streamliner and Endeavour each interpret the 30-second display differently.The trio combines exposed mechanics, fumé dials and automatic calibers with three-day reserves.H. Moser & Cie. is expanding its retrograde seconds concept across three of its core collections with the new Pioneer Skeleton Retrograde Seconds, Streamliner Retrograde Seconds and Endeavour Retrograde Seconds. Following the success of the original Pioneer Retrograde Seconds, the trio takes the same theatrical idea - a seconds hand travelling across a 30-second arc before snapping instantly back to zero - and gives it three distinct personalities. The mechanism itself is deliberately exposed on the dial, where a double snail cam, rack and hairspring coordinate the hand’s repeated journey, accompanied by a two-tone indicator showing whether the watch is within the first or second half of each minute.The Pioneer Skeleton Retrograde Seconds offers the most mechanical interpretation, placing the complication within a fully openworked 40mm steel case where anthracite bridges and wheels contrast against gold-toned hands and markers. Its fully skeletonized HMC 251 automatic caliber integrates the retrograde mechanism directly and delivers a minimum three-day power reserve, while a steel bracelet and additional khaki rubber strap reinforce its sport-watch positioning.The Streamliner Retrograde Seconds takes a smoother approach, pairing the display at 6 o’clock with the collection’s fluid 40mm steel case, integrated bracelet and Midnight Blue fumé sunburst dial. Here, the automatic HMC 252 caliber combines Moser’s base movement with a 30-second retrograde module developed by Agenhor, maintaining the same minimum three-day reserve while letting the hand’s sudden reset interrupt the otherwise flowing architecture.Completing the trio, the Endeavour Retrograde Seconds translates the complication into Moser’s most understated format. Its 40mm steel case frames a Blackor fumé sunburst dial, with the exposed retrograde mechanism at 6 o’clock adding controlled visual tension beneath the collection’s otherwise minimalist display. Like the Streamliner, it uses the HMC 252 automatic caliber and is finished with a night-blue nubuck alligator strap, keeping the overall presentation more formal.The trio is priced between $35,200 USD and $44,100 USD. For more information, head over to H. Moser & Cie.'s official website and boutiques.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: BAIT x G-SHOCK Went Bananas on the "Yamagata's Finest" DW5600
Entertainment.text: SummaryG-SHOCK and BAIT reunite on the DW5600 with "Yamagata's Finest," a release that pays tribute to the Japanese prefecture where G-SHOCK production beginsThe design takes its cue from a banana at peak ripeness, a playful nod to timing that suits both a watch and a long-running partnershipCustom can-and-box packaging introduces "Shawty with Freckles," a mascot built to represent the shared culture behind the collaborationG-SHOCK and BAIT have returned to the DW5600 for "Yamagata's Finest," a banana-themed take on the classic square that honors Yamagata Prefecture, the home of Casio's Premium Production Line. Billed as a "non-GMO" edition, the collaboration trades outside references for a tribute to the place where every G-SHOCK gets its start.The watch commits fully to its fruit theme. The case and strap are finished in a saturated banana yellow, framing a light gray face plate that surrounds a blue-tinted digital display showing the day, date and time. The bezel keeps the DW5600's familiar layout, with "PROTECTION" printed across the top and "G-SHOCK" lettering along the bottom in a muted contrast tone. Small dark flecks scattered across the strap appear to mimic the sugar spots that show up on a banana just as it hits its sweetest point.That ripeness is the core joke. A banana at its peak is all about timing, which makes it a neat fit for a watch and, as the partners frame it, for two brands coming back together at the right moment. The yellow-on-gray palette keeps the concept legible at a glance without leaning on graphics, letting the color do the storytelling.The packaging extends the bit. Rather than a standard G-SHOCK box, the watch arrives in a special can and box carrying "Shawty with Freckles," a makeshift mascot positioned as the face of the partnership and a symbol of the cultural common ground between BAIT and Casio. In the press imagery, the character appears on a blue oval badge styled like a produce sticker, complete with a script "Shawty" logo.The deeper story sits in Yamagata. The prefecture houses Casio's Premium Production Line and the factory where G-SHOCK production begins, making it a fitting focal point for a collaboration about origins. Casio's facility there, Yamagata Casio in Higashine, is also known for producing the brand's high-end MR-G and MT-G models. The DW5600 itself traces its lineage to the original DW-5000C, the shock-resistant square that launched G-SHOCK in 1983, so pairing the model with its manufacturing home brings the release full circle.The G-SHOCK x BAIT "Yamagata's Finest" DW5600 is available now online.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Rise of the Tomb Raider: 20 Year Collection Swings to Physical on Nintendo Switch 2 from Limited Run Games.
Entertainment.text: SummaryAspyr and Limited Run Games are bringing Rise of the Tomb Raider: 20 Year Collection to Nintendo Switch 2 as a physical release in Standard and Collector's EditionsEach version includes the base game alongside the "Blood Ties" and "Lara's Nightmare" stories, the online Co-Op Endurance mode and the "Extreme Survivor" difficultyThe Collector's Edition adds a SteelCase, a Trinity cloth patch and a light-up replica of the game's "Divine Source" artifactAspyr and Limited Run Games are taking Rise of the Tomb Raider: 20 Year Collection to the Nintendo Switch 2, issuing Lara Croft's Siberian adventure as a physical release in both Standard and Collector's Edition formats. Each package includes a physical Game Card loaded with the full game and its Season Pass content, giving Switch 2 players the complete version of one of the franchise's most celebrated modern entries.The title has been around for just over a decade. Crystal Dynamics first released Rise of the Tomb Raider in 2015 as the sequel to its 2013 reboot, then expanded it into the "20 Year Celebration" edition in 2016 to mark two decades since the original Tomb Raider debuted in 1996. That anniversary branding carries over to this release even as the franchise itself now sits at 30 years old. Aspyr, which handles development on the Switch 2 version, has recent history with the series, having also overseen 2024's Tomb Raider I–III Remastered.The story follows Lara into the frozen wilds of Siberia in search of Kitezh, a lost city tied to the Divine Source, an artifact believed to grant immortality. Standing in her way is Trinity, a shadowy organization chasing the same prize. Kitezh draws on a real Russian legend of a city that vanished beneath a lake to escape invaders, giving the expedition a mythic anchor.Gameplay splits time between survival, combat and puzzle-solving. Players hunt wildlife and gather scarce materials to craft weapons and gear in hostile terrain, then put that kit to work in open-ended encounters where Lara can climb trees, slip underwater, set traps and improvise explosives. Her compound bow and climbing axe remain the core tools, and loadouts can be tuned for anything from quiet takedowns to full firefights. Optional tombs return in a bigger way, packing large chambers with lethal traps, environmental puzzles and ancient texts that point toward hidden crypts.The Season Pass content fills out the package. "Blood Ties" opens up Croft Manor for a story-driven exploration of Lara's family history, while "Lara's Nightmare" turns the same estate into a zombie defense scenario. "Baba Yaga: The Temple of the Witch" sends players into a new tomb built around the Slavic folklore figure, and "Cold Darkness Awakened" throws waves of infected enemies into the mix. Rounding things out are the online Co-Op Endurance mode, the punishing "Extreme Survivor" difficulty, five classic Lara skins and an outfit and weapon inspired by 1998's Tomb Raider III.On the physical side, the Standard Edition keeps things simple with the Game Card, a game case and an eight-page booklet. The Collector's Edition builds on that with a dedicated outer box, a SteelCase, a Trinity cloth patch and the standout piece: a light-up desk ornament modeled after the Divine Source.Pre-orders for the Standard and Collector's Editions of Rise of the Tomb Raider: 20 Year Collection on Nintendo Switch 2 open October 9.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: New Wi-Fi Alliance Certifications Hint at an Upcoming PlayStation Portal OLED
Entertainment.text: SummaryThe Wi-Fi Alliance certified two unannounced PlayStation devices classified as gaming peripheralsCertification documents reveal the new hardware models run on the Android 15 operating systemHardware leaks suggest Sony is preparing an OLED version of its streaming handheldThe Wi-Fi Alliance recently certified a pair of unannounced PlayStation devices, signaling an imminent hardware update that appears to be an iteration of the PlayStation Portal handheld. According to the official certification documents, the two new products are formally classified as "Gaming Console/Peripherals." The fresh hardware operates under the model numbers CFI-Y2000 and CFI-Y2105. That specific numbering sequence directly follows the CFI-Y1001 model number utilized by the currently available PlayStation Portal. The original PlayStation Portal officially launched in late 2023, and these freshly certified models appear poised to serve as direct updates to that dedicated remote-play platform. PlayStation did not immediately reply to a request for comment regarding the recent Wi-Fi Alliance certifications.Technical specifications provided by the certification documents show that the newly certified models run on the Android 15 operating system. This software architecture mirrors the current PlayStation Portal model, which also operates on Android. Relying on an Android foundation contrasts with heavier flagship hardware, as the PS5 home console natively runs on a custom operating system. Network capabilities for the unannounced gadgets remain familiar, as they are officially certified for 1x1 2.4GHz and 5GHz Wi-Fi. The new devices are not certified for 6GHz Wi-Fi, and the certified hardware does not feature more Wi-Fi antennas than the previous model.Earlier this year, hardware leaker KeplerL2 stated that Sony was actively working on "another version" of the Portal. The leaker claimed the new device would arrive as an OLED version, upgrading the original PlayStation Portal that currently features an 8-inch LCD screen. Keeping the identical networking specifications while upgrading the screen aligns with the company's broader hardware strategy. Sony noted in June that cloud streaming requires minimal memory, framing thin client devices as an attractive, low-cost option amid rising memory prices. Iterating on a low-memory thin client with an upgraded OLED panel allows the brand to dodge volatile memory costs while keeping the streaming ecosystem visually competitive.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: HOMEGAME and New Era’s "Kasane Pack" Layers Traditional Japanese Patterns Onto MLB Crowns
Entertainment.text: SummaryHOMEGAME and New Era rework three MLB 59FIFTY fitteds with crowns cut from fabric that combines several traditional Japanese motifsEach team is assigned its own color story, with blue for the Dodgers, green for the Mariners and purple for the YankeesPattern placement shifts from cap to cap, so no two pieces in the pack look exactly alikeHOMEGAME and New Era have teamed up on the 59FIFTY "Kasane Pack," a three-piece MLB capsule built from patchwork-style fabric that pulls together a range of traditional Japanese patterns. The Japan-based cap specialist gave each team its own palette, matching the Los Angeles Dodgers, Seattle Mariners and New York Yankees with tonal prints and coordinating visors.The starting point is the textile. Rather than printing a single graphic, the pack uses a fabric that assembles several classic Japanese motifs and botanical references into one surface. Three stand out: the geometric asanoha, or hemp leaf, grid; clusters of small, delicate flowers; and upright stalks of bamboo. HOMEGAME pitches the project as a modern reconstruction of these centuries-old designs, with attention paid from the choice of cloth through to how it's cut and set onto the six-panel crown.Each colorway gets a name drawn from its dominant hue and motif. "AIKA" (藍花) dresses the Dodgers cap in blue-toned prints with a solid blue brim. "SUIMA" (翠麻) shifts the Mariners version into greens and finishes it with a Northwest Green visor. "SHICHIKU" (紫竹) gives the Yankees edition a purple-leaning crown set against a navy brim.The trims hold steady across all three. Team logos (LA, S and NY) sit up front in raised 3D embroidery, while MLB's Batterman logo anchors the rear. Inside, a white sweatband lines the crown, and a gray undervisor runs beneath every brim, keeping the busy outer fabric grounded with a clean, classic base.Because the patterned cloth is cut panel by panel, the motifs land differently on every cap. One Yankees fitted might put a bamboo stalk front and center while the next leads with hemp leaf geometry, which makes each piece effectively one of a kind. It's a fitting detail for a pairing between New Era, the 1920-founded headwear label that serves as MLB's sole official on-field cap supplier, and HOMEGAME, a shop known for stocking New Era styles unreleased in Japan alongside its own hip-hop-leaning "HOMEGAME CUSTOM" makeups.The New Era x HOMEGAME 59FIFTY "Kasane Pack" drops October 10 at HOMEGAME stores and via the HOMEGAME online store.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming Is the Only Platform That Can Stream 'GTA VI' at Launch
Entertainment.text: SummaryMicrosoft has secured exclusive launch streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI via Xbox Cloud GamingRockstar Games has not yet announced a native PC version of the highly anticipated titleXbox is launching pay-as-you-go access and enforcing new monthly hourly streaming caps to monetize the cloud surgeXbox CEO Asha Sharma has confirmed to staff that Microsoft is preparing an initiative for Grand Theft Auto VI that no other platform holder is currently matching. Sources familiar with the company's internal roadmap confirmed that Microsoft has officially secured exclusive launch streaming rights for the title. Under this agreement, Xbox Cloud Gaming is the only platform permitted to stream the game at launch. The exact length of this exclusivity deal remains unknown.This exclusivity deal directly targets PC players. Because publisher Rockstar Games has not yet announced a native PC version of the game, players without a console face a potential hardware upgrade. The streaming arrangement allows Microsoft to offer Xbox Cloud Gaming to PC users who would otherwise need to buy an Xbox Series X, an Xbox Series S or a PS5 console.To prepare for this launch, Microsoft is restructuring its access pipeline before Grand Theft Auto VI releases in November. The company is debuting a pay-as-you-go pricing tier for Xbox Cloud Gaming alongside the game's release. This model allows players without a console or an active subscription to access the game on mobile devices by purchasing individual bundles of streaming hours. Such transactional pricing positions Microsoft to monetize users who do not want a recurring monthly subscription.Managing the expected wave of traffic requires Microsoft to also end unlimited streaming for existing Xbox Game Pass subscribers in November. The company will enforce strict monthly limits on gameplay hours. Under the new rules, Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers are capped at 15 streaming hours per month. Those on the Xbox Game Pass Premium tier are limited to 10 streaming hours per month, while Xbox Game Pass Essential subscribers are restricted to five hours.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Other.title: Carhartt WIP x Kinto's Kakomi Donabe Puts the Japanese Clay Pot to Work
Other.text: SummaryCarhartt WIP and Japanese lifestyle brand Kinto team up on the Kakomi Donabe, a contemporary update of the traditional Japanese cooking potThe ceramic body handles open flame, microwave and oven heat, while a stainless steel plate lets it double as a steamerThe pot holds 2.5 liters and arrives in a Black/Grey colorway finished with a graphic printCarhartt WIP and Kinto have joined forces on the Kakomi Donabe, a modern reworking of the Japanese clay cooking pot finished in Black/Grey. Instead of treating the donabe as a delicate heirloom piece, the collaboration rebuilds it as a hardwearing kitchen tool that moves between cooking methods with minimal fuss.The biggest change is the material. Where the traditional donabe is shaped from clay, this version is made from a heat-resistant ceramic, giving it the range to sit directly over a flame, slide into the oven or go into the microwave. That versatility carries through to cleanup, as the pot is dishwasher safe.Size-wise, the Kakomi Donabe holds 2,500 milliliters (about 85 ounces) and measures 27.5 x 14.5 x 31.5 centimeters (10.8 x 5.7 x 12.4 inches), putting it firmly in the territory of a shared, table-centered vessel rather than a single-serving cooker.A stainless steel steam plate is included in the box, so the pot can be used for steaming in addition to simmering. The metal insert pairs the ceramic body with a second material that suits the brand's utilitarian leanings while expanding what the pot can actually do.Visually, the piece keeps things restrained. The Black/Grey colorway gives the ceramic a muted, workshop-ready tone, and a graphic print finishes the exterior. Kinto, a Japanese label known for refined everyday goods spanning water bottles, kitchenware and specialty coffee equipment, brings its homeware know-how to the build.The Carhartt WIP x Kinto Kakomi Donabe is listed as coming soon via Carhartt WIP's online store.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Million Goods Brings Its Menswear, Hi-Fi and Natural Wine Concept to Fort Greene, Brooklyn
Art & Culture.text: SummaryMillion Goods has opened its second location, in Fort Greene, BrooklynThe space includes two custom sound systems split across a ground floor bar and listening room, and an upstairs retail floorThe store stocks brands like Nicholas Daley, OAMC Peacemaker, Soulland, Rold Skov, LC23, Berner Kühl, Ranra and sssteinMillion Goods, a Brooklyn-based retail concept combining independent menswear, hi-fi, natural wine and cultural programming, has opened its second location in Fort Greene, Brooklyn. A roughly 2,100-square-foot space set inside a landmarked building, the new location ports the brand's DNA from its original Greenpoint location further south in the borough. Founders Drew Kaufmann and Matt Reyer treated the project as an adaptive reuse, keeping the building's tin ceilings, fireplaces, wood floors and spiral staircase rather than gutting the interior. The store is split into three areas of about 700 square feet each: a bar and listening room on the lower level, a retail floor upstairs and a garden at the rear, visible from the entrance through large windows at the back of the listening floor.The original spiral staircase connecting the two floors is now wrapped in red metalwork, while other details like pecan finished woodwork, honed stone surfaces and limewash paint compliment custom aluminum retail fixtures. Louis Poulsen PH 5 pendants and AJ Eklipta wall lamps illuminate the space while the sound comes Bridge Street Sound designed slim-profile speakers and Million Goods-developed dual-sided speakers, both tuned by Ojas collaborator and sound designer Mo Yasin.The upstairs retail floor carries labels including Nicholas Daley, OAMC Peacemaker, Soulland, Rold Skov, LC23, Berner Kühl, Ranra and ssstein, with Kaufmann and Reyer selecting pieces directly with each brand. Downstairs, the natural wine list centers on France, the Fort Greene location serving a broader by-the-glass selection than Greenpoint. Out back, the garden incorporates the existing trees into the built-in seating with a layout that references Brazilian Brutalism and Japanese garden design.Million Goods Fort Greene is now open Tuesday through Sunday from noon until 10 p.m. on Tuesdays and Sundays, 11 p.m. on Wednesdays, and 12 a.m. on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays. The original Greenpoint store continues to operate at 88 Franklin Street.>Million Goods Fort Greene201 DeKalb AvenueFort Greene, BrooklynNew York CityClick here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
